Straight answers

Questions people actually ask

Short answers, with the guide or framework layer that goes deeper linked from most of them. Nothing here is a substitute for a written answer from your district bureau.

Eligibility

Can a foreigner buy property in China?

Yes. A foreign national may buy one self-use residential property, in the city where they work or study, after at least one year of working or studying in China. You cannot buy land, and you cannot own more than one home. The practical checks are run by the district housing bureau, not by a national office.

How many properties can a foreigner own?

One self-use home nationwide, in the city where you work or study. A spouse's existing Chinese property counts against the household, so a marriage to a Chinese national who already owns a home can block a purchase. There is no route to a second home for personal use.

Do I need to live in China to buy?

Effectively yes. The one-year work or study requirement, plus the requirement to buy in the city of employment, means non-resident buyers are excluded in practice. A few specialist structures exist for companies and institutional investors, but they are not designed for individuals.

Can I buy on a tourist visa?

No. You need a residence permit that reflects work or study, and evidence of at least a year of it. A tourist or business visa does not satisfy the requirement, and the housing bureau will check the permit type, not just its validity.

Can I buy commercial property or an office?

Not as an individual in most cities. Commercial and office units are generally transacted through companies, and 40- or 50-year commercial-residential units (商住) are closed to foreign individual buyers in most markets. If a seller tells you otherwise, get it in writing from the district bureau before paying anything.

Can my company buy a home for me to live in?

A China-registered company can own property, but the purchase is treated as a business asset, not a self-use home, which brings tax and disclosure consequences. Using a company to sidestep the individual one-home rule is a structure that is examined and frequently unwound at resale.

Money

How much deposit is normal?

One to five per cent of price is typical for resale, paid against a written deposit agreement. Off-plan purchases usually require a deposit plus a staged payment schedule. Never pay a deposit before your lawyer has seen the title search and the contract, and never pay it into a personal account.

Can a foreigner get a mortgage in China?

Yes, from a subset of banks. Expect loan-to-value of 50–60%, a term capped by age, and stricter income documentation than a citizen would face. Your nationality, where your income is earned, and whether you already own property in China all change the answer.

What taxes will I pay when I buy?

Deed tax is the main one: 1% for homes up to 140m² (first or second home), 1.5–2% above that. Add agency commission around 1%, notarisation in some cities, and registration fees. Budget 3–6% on top of the purchase price.

Can I send the money back out when I sell?

Yes, in principle, through the banking system with a documented trail. You will need the original purchase documentation, tax receipts, and the sale contract. The practical difficulty scales with how well your inbound funds were documented, which is why the paper trail matters more than the exit itself.

Transaction

How long does a purchase take?

Resale typically takes six to ten weeks from accepted offer to registration, assuming a clean title and cash payment. Add four to eight weeks if a mortgage is involved. Off-plan is a different timeline: two to three years to handover is normal.

Do I need a lawyer?

It is not legally required, but buying without independent counsel is the single most expensive shortcut foreign buyers take. A title search and a contract review cost a fraction of one percentage point of the purchase price, and they are the only part of the process where someone is unambiguously on your side.

What is 网签 and why does it matter?

It is the online contract registration that locks the transaction into the housing authority's system. Once a sale is 网签, the same unit cannot be sold to someone else. It is also the point at which your identity and eligibility are formally checked, so do not treat it as paperwork to do later.

What happens if the seller backs out?

Usually the deposit is returned double, if the deposit agreement says so — which is why the wording matters. In practice, enforcement means negotiation or litigation, and litigation over a residential sale takes months to years. Structure the deposit and the escrow so that walking away is expensive for the seller.

Living

Can I rent out the home I buy?

Yes, as a private landlord. You should register the lease with the local housing authority, pay the relevant tax, and ensure the tenant completes address registration. Short-term letting through platforms is a different and more heavily regulated activity.

Do I need to register my address?

Yes. Foreign nationals must complete residence registration (住宿登记) at the local police station after moving in, and again after any change of address. Hotels do it for you; private accommodation does not. A missing registration can complicate visa renewal, banking and school applications.

Can my family inherit the property?

Yes, including a foreign spouse or child, but the process is administrative and slow: notarisation of the inheritance, then registration of the transfer. The heir must generally be able to hold the asset under the same rules, and selling an inherited property as a foreign national brings its own tax and repatriation questions.
